name: Watermelon Anthracnose
description: A fungal disease causing sunken lesions on watermelon leaves, stems, and fruits. It is seed-borne and can cause significant fruit quality deterioration and yield loss.
symptoms: Circular yellow water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown
Dark sunken lesions on stems and petioles
Pink spore masses in lesion centers under humid conditions
Fruit lesions as circular sunken spots with pink centers
Fruit rot and cracking at lesion sites
causes: Infected seeds serving as inoculum source
treatments: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb at first symptoms
Spray azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin for systemic control
Use copper-based fungicides as preventive treatment
Remove and destroy severely infected plant parts
prevention: Treat seeds with hot water (50°C for 30 minutes) before planting
Practice crop rotation with non-cucurbit crops
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
